items.title: Charles Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I was listening to something from a record you did years later in ’72, it happened to have one of my favorite drummers Alvin Queen on it, and the record was “Impact.”

ctx.x: Well he was 24, 23, 24. And me 21 or 22 you know.

Yeah. Very exciting. So I was listening to something from a record you did years later in ’72, it happened to have one of my favorite drummers Alvin Queen on it, and the record was “Impact.” And I’m curious if the rehearsal time and recording time, how it compared to your first experience with Jackie McLean. Did you have more time, less time?
Well that was a live recording.

items.title: Alvin Queen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 23, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I got a call one day from Charles Tolliver during my stint with George Benson in 1971, to go to Europe.

ctx.x: What would it have required of you to do that?

Well I first went to — I never had any dreams really, as far as going to Europe. And I basically always wanted to be involved with different groups and to build my own group. And I spent many, many years as you know, with Horace Silver and George Benson and Wild Bill Davis and Tiny Grimes, and I mean I can go back, oh, Pharoah Sanders — I’ve done some stuff with George Coleman’s recordings, and many different people. And I got a call one day from Charles Tolliver during my stint with George Benson in 1971, to go…
there than I worked in America. And that’s the reason why I travel so much. But I made my — my biggest communication, I believe, was in Europe with the musicians. That’s how I managed to do that.

items.title: Alvin Queen interviewed by Monk Row, via Zoom, July 21, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: When I came to Europe I came to Europe with Charles Tolliver and I did stuff with Benny Wallace, Eddie Gomez and all of them.

ctx.x: I know you like a challenge. Do you have a personal view on why this pandemic occurred in 2020 at this moment?

Well there’s a lot of distortion on earth. It’s not all — you can’t, see the first thing you can’t see everything from America, and there’s a lot of people in North America that know more than people in the south of America. Okay? You can go to Alabama, you can go to those states, a lot of them wouldn’t even know what’s going on. But you have pollution, you’ve got destruction, you’ve got military weapons. You’ve got all kinds of stuff. And it’s all over the world. You notice that it’s not only one country…

we have Ciba Geigy here. Okay? One of the biggest pharmaceutical medicine makers. You look at New Jersey, look what’s going in the air. Look what you’re breathing you see? And I don’t believe that it’s one virus. I believe it’s a combination of many things going on you see. And it’s just that we are human beings but what’s going on on the earth is getting smarter than who we are.
